bipartite.kami_theme: The speaker has tried to conceal a secret love, but it has visibly shown on his face/complexion despite his effort at concealment.
bipartite.shimo_theme: Others have noticed this outward sign and now directly ask him whether he is troubled by some hidden longing.
bipartite.pivot_note: The kami-no-ku states the internal effort (concealment) and its involuntary physical betrayal (color showing on the face); the shimo-no-ku reveals the social consequence — other people's direct inquiry — which functions as external proof that the concealment in kami has failed. The turn is from private failure of will to public exposure through others' perception, making the whole poem a single continuous causal chain: secrecy → betrayal of countenance → others noticing → being asked directly.

kigo.note: Though 色 ('color, complexion') might evoke autumn foliage imagery elsewhere in the canon, here it is used purely in the psychological-physiognomic sense ('one's countenance betraying inner feeling'), a stock phrase in love poetry (koi no uta) rather than a seasonal image. No genuine seasonal word is present in this poem; it belongs to the koi (love) topic-category of the Hyakunin Isshu rather than any of the four seasons.

source_jp:
忍ぶれど
色に出でにけり
わが恋は
物や思ふと
人の問ふまで
